newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire government says still seeks peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Zaire government says still seeks peace talks.

text.p: The government of Zaire said on Wednesday that it was still seeking a peaceful solution to the country's civil war and did not believe that the peace process had broken down because of rebel leader Laurent Kabila's failure to show up for talks aboard a South African naval ship.
"We do not think that the talks have broken down," government spokesman Kin-Kiey Mulumba told reporters in Kinshasha.
Zaire government says still seeks peace talks

News that Kabila had demanded the talks be held on the high seas to guarantee his security and that South African president Nelson Mandela, as mediator, had rejected the demand sparked rumours in Kinshasha that the fragile peace process was finished.

"We are for national pacification and reconciliation," Mulumba said. "...The government supports and encourages the peace process that began in Pretoria (where South Africa first brought together representatives of the two sides, in March).
The government spokesman said that Mobutu preferred the logic of peace "but if the logic of war continues we will take that into account".

Contrary to rebel "propaganda" he said the Zairean army was fighting with courage and determination and the war front had stabilised some 200 km (120 miles) east of the capital, with no advance and no threat to Kinshasha airport or the city itself.
